title: Female student admitted to medical school after overcoming nine near-death experiences.
excerpt: More than five years after battling bone cancer, Hoang Thi Linh Nhi (20 years old) was accepted into the medical field, officially donning a white lab coat.
content:
Linh Nhi was admitted to the Medical program and received a lab coat from Professor, Doctor Tran Trung Dung at the opening ceremony.

At the end of September, during the opening ceremony of the 2026-2027 academic year at VinUni University, Hoang Thi Linh Nhi was presented with a white lab coat by Professor, Doctor Tran Trung Dung (an expert in the field of Orthopedic Trauma Surgery).

Over five years ago, Professor, Doctor Dung was the one who performed the total femur replacement surgery on Nhi. Now, the girl who has undergone nine surgeries and "escaped death" has officially become a medical student.

9 surgeries to treat cancer

Linh Nhi grew up in the former Ba Ria - Vung Tau province . In November 2018, the 7th-grade girl fractured her right femur after a jump during physical education class. Initially, Nhi thought it was just a common injury. However, after surgery to remove bone for cell testing, the biopsy results showed that Nhi had osteosarcoma - a type of bone cancer.

Nhi's parents hid her illness, only saying she had osteoporosis. But one day, while looking at a medical bill, she accidentally saw her name along with the diagnosis. "That's when I found out I had cancer," Nhi recalled.

At the age of 12, Nhi couldn't fully comprehend what she was about to go through. Through television and newspapers, she only knew that cancer was a serious disease. While her peers were running, jumping, and playing, she could only lie in one place. Some nights, Nhi thought a lot, and there were times when she wanted to give up.

The successive rounds of chemotherapy left her body completely exhausted. Nhi feared she would become a burden to her family. But seeing her parents' efforts to get treatment, she told herself that sadness wouldn't solve anything. "Whatever the solution, I'll fight along with the doctors," Nhi recounted.

After chemotherapy, the tumor responded to the medication. However, to save her life, the doctor announced that the best option was to amputate her leg. Seeing her mother cry so much, Nhi felt very sorry for her. She proactively encouraged her mother, saying, "As long as I live, that's all that matters; what I look like doesn't matter."

Fortunately, the doctors then offered another option: bone growth therapy. The cancerous part of the bone was removed, and then a system of metal pins and plates was used to fix and allow the bone to grow longer. This method carried many risks, but it could save her leg, so the girl didn't want to miss the chance.

"When I woke up after the surgery, I saw a huge cage attached to my leg from end to end," Nhi recounted, saying that she has been bedridden ever since.

However, after 17 months of immobilization, this method proved ineffective due to bone infection, requiring removal to preserve the remaining bone. Nhi was taken to Hanoi by her father to see Dr. Dung. In 19 days, the girl underwent two major surgeries to remove and implant a metal knee joint.

Chân Linh Nhi after having her femur replaced with an artificial bone.

But the infection persisted. Nhi's leg became swollen, abscesses appeared, and the infection spread to her hip joint. She underwent three more surgeries at the Children's Hospital of Ho Chi Minh City to clean the infected area around the metal joint.

In early 2021, after consultation, Dr. Dung and his team agreed on a plan to replace Linh Nhi's entire femur. However, before this surgery, the 15-year-old girl had to undergo another operation to remove the old joint.

A few days after her historic total femur replacement surgery, Nhi was able to stand up and try to walk. But the physical therapy process after a long period of immobility was "the most painful experience." Putting her body weight on her leg caused Nhi "unbearable pain."

Even so, the 15-year-old girl didn't shed a single tear. "I want to go. To walk on my own two feet," the student shared about her motivation.

The journey to fulfilling the dream of becoming a doctor.

Over two years of treatment also interrupted Nhi's studies. Initially, she tried tutoring, self-studying via YouTube, and borrowing friends' notebooks to copy notes. But the chemotherapy sessions left her body exhausted, constantly anemic, and unable to absorb knowledge, so Nhi's parents had to request a two-year deferment of her studies.

After recovering from her illness, Nhi asked her parents if she could resume her studies from the 7th grade to consolidate her knowledge. The time spent in the hospital bed was also when her dream of becoming a doctor began to take shape. Each time she entered the operating room, instead of being anxious or afraid of medical instruments, Nhi would often show curiosity and excitement, asking the doctors about needles, IV lines, and surgical equipment.

"When doctors ask me if I'm interested in this field, I always say yes," Nhi recounted.

But after nine surgeries and numerous anesthesia sessions, Nhi found that her memory and reflexes were no longer as sharp as before. Frequent anemia also affected her ability to concentrate. To remember her lessons, the student had to take careful notes and reread them many times.

Despite this, Nhi maintained excellent academic results. In grades 10 and 11, she was an outstanding student, and in grade 12, she was an excellent student. Nhi also won an honorable mention in the city-level Biology competition for outstanding students and achieved an IELTS score of 7.0.

After the high school graduation exam, following Dr. Dung's suggestion, Nhi researched and applied to VinUni. The female student was accepted into the Medical Doctor program and received a 50% scholarship.

Linh Nhi and her father on her first day of university.

More than two months after starting university, Nhi had gradually become accustomed to student life, and daily routines were not difficult. Every morning, she woke up at 7 a.m., had breakfast, and walked from the dormitory to the lecture hall. Outside of class, she participated in discussions and completed group assignments.

During her first semester, Nhi studied many subjects such as Political Economy, Social Sciences, Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Human Biology, Nutrition, and Communication in the Health Community. Compared to high school, the female student had to proactively manage her time, read materials, and complete assignments.

Currently, Nhi's health is stable. The student only needs to have regular check-ups every six months for X-rays and monitoring of her bone condition. From a girl who once thought simply staying alive was a blessing, Nhi is now taking steps closer to her dream of becoming a doctor.

"The path to studying medicine will be challenging, but compared to the time I spent battling illness, I think I have enough perseverance to pursue this choice," Nhi shared.
